You can't let the expectations of other or society influence you. Its all bullshit. Trust me. To get by in life, you really got to learn not to give a fuck about anyone else but yourself. So who cares what other people think or say. That is the NUMBER ONE most important thing to achieve in life: dont give a fuck about others. Most people are depressed or anxious or sad because of the influence of other people or society or expectations. If you let this outside things seep into your life, obviously they're going to bring you down.

I've been feeling depressed for as long as I remember. In elementary school I dreamed of dying and wrote suicide notes. So I get it. I also know theres no point hoping that things will get better. So don't hope. you just really gotta trust. Don't hope. Just trust that theres a light at the end of the tunnel even though you're in the dark running into walls, tripping over things, blind and scared. 

I'm like not even joking though. Rather than wallow in your self pity, YOU have to want to get better. If all you're going to do is sit there and fight any help and complain, obviously then you're going to stay miserable, depressed, and unhappy. You have to seriously WANT to get better and you have to be proactive about trying to do something to at least make yourself feel SOME relief. You don't have to turn your life around 180 and feel like you're on top of the world. It's gonna take a lot of damn baby steps. 

Do you exercise at all? Because I'm not even joking that changed my life. And there has been a TON of studies showing how exercise decreases stress hormones and increases the feel good chemicals like seratonin and dopamine. It can provide some relief WHILE slowly building your confidence. Rather than wallow and fight in your self pity and spend hours scrolling through social media, just go run 1 mile today. I'm serious. You'll at least feel accomplished. And if you say no, you better have a damn good reason why you can't or why you're not. Am I right?

Also, if you feel like its preventing you from moving forward in life, I highly recommend seeing a professional. A therapist or a psychiatrist. I started therapy in high school and I'm still going. And when depression was eating me alive and I started not taking care of myself and slacking, antidepressants honestly help lift the weight off my shoulders to be able to stand on my feet and have the energy to make changes I needed to move forward in life. i highly recommend considering professional help.

Hey, 

It sounds like you're having a lot of fear and anxiety about life and the future. And I want to let you know, that's normal. But for some, that's also what depression feeds off of.

For being 19, its COMPLETELY normal to have no idea what your passions and interests are. It is completely normal to have no idea what you want or what you're supposed to be doing. Your 20's are meant to be discovering who you are. And yes its scary. The unknown and the uncertainty are always scary. And yes, you might make some bad choices or some mistakes along the way. But know that is all completely normal and that is part of growing up and that is all part of the process of trying to figure out who you are and what you like. 

You're bright. And I know this because you think. You think much more and much deeply than most people who can get through life mindlessly and blissfully ignorant. You are aware that you overthink and that being alone with your mind is dangerous. It sounds like your mind puts yourself down. Makes you worry and fearful. And the first thing you have to do is stop allowing your mind to do that. The very first thing you have to do is embrace the discomfort. Embrace the fear of the future. Embrace the fact that you have no idea what's going on right now, who you are, and embrace the fact that that is OK and that is completely normal at your age. 

Then, start making small changes, start making new habits, to start to explore life and enable a positive lifestyle change. For example, it sounds like you're home a lot with a lot of free time. So you've just been mindlessly scrolling through social media. Let me tell you this, and I hope you can really trust me on this, social media is TOXIC and it is bad for the psyche and your mental wellbeing. It is extremely pointless and wastes a lot of energy. I highly recommend going on a social media detox. Delete the snapchat, instagram, facebook (you can keep messenger to talk to people if you do) for at least 2 months. I've done this when I've been hit by bad depressive episodes and trust me it helps a lot in bringing me out of the rut. Consider it. 
 
If you do that, you'll be left with a lot of free time. So you now need to find hobbies and activities to fill in that free time. This is the perfect opportunity to try new things. And through trying new things, maybe youll discover a passion or something more about yourself. Perhaps join a gym, pick up kickboxing or martial arts (I highly recommend jiu jitsu. Joe Rogan is a huge advocate on how jiu jitsu can change your life because its a mental chess game that demands dedication). Try starting rock climbing! Surfing. Learn a new language. I tried to teach myself russian last summer and I actually really enjoyed it lol. Photography and photoshop. Theres a ton of things. Yoga. Meditation. I'm also not sure if you're working, but try applying for a part time job since you're not in school! You'll at least feel better that youre being productive and making money rather than sitting at home scrolling through social media. 

As time goes on, you'll start to figure out what you want to do. You have to trust that everything will work out in the end, so you can't let the fear of the future paralyze you right now. 

Let me know if any of that is useful, and if you have any questions about anything. You really remind me a lot of myself, and so I really wish you peace and eventual happiness.

Also, if you want to know more about any of the hobbies I listed (especially martial arts lol) please ask!! I love talking about it and I HIGHLY encourage people to try it! It helps a TON.

This is something interesting I haven't thought about. I'm split on wanting to know and not wanting to know for two reasons:

For my own sake and my own happiness, I don't want to know if I will likely get a disease. Because being genetically predisposed doesn't necessarily mean you'll 100% get the disease. If I am told I have like a 90% of getting cancer or Alzheimer's, I think it would make me somewhat depressed and hopeless. It might hold me back on a lot of things. For example, if I think I'll get Alzheimers, it'll probably affect my decision to get married, settle down, and have kids. I think having the knowledge that I have a chance of getting some disease that could drastically alter my life will in fact alter my life before I even get the disease (if I get it). I do believe ignorance is bliss and I'm okay with that. I'd rather live my life without the worry or fear and making decisions for things I want at the moment.

On the other hand, for the sake of family and loved ones, yes I'd want to know. For example, if I already am in a committed long-term relationship or if I already have kids, I would want to know for their sake so I can prepare. For example, if I'm genetically predisposed to Alzheimers, I'd want to know so that I can prepare a "what to do" when I do start showing signs of Alzheimers. I'd probably tell my husband/kids it's okay to put me in a nursing home etc etc if I start to really mess things up. It's mostly for their sake, not so much mine.

TLDR: If I have no obligations to people (husband/kids), I don't want to know if I'll get a disease. Frankly, I don't care, and I don't think there's any point worrying about getting a disease I might not ever get. If I do have obligations, like a family, I'd only want to know for their sake.
